records.title: RLUSD on the XRP Ledger: 99.6% of its payments were 110 bots — PoR label passage re-read
records.summary: A fresh line-by-line review confirms Bitquery explicitly says its XRPL exchange labels are drawn from exchanges' published proof-of-reserves lists (article lines 84 and 156), and specifically states that rDAE53VfMvftPB4ogpWGWvzkQxfht6JPxr is labeled Binance in the exchange's proof-of-reserves list (line 180). The same investigation says rDAE53 funded 109 wallets with 13,341 RLUSD in 1,431 payments, while six other Binance-labelled wallets supplied 5,419 XRP to the cluster; collector sweeps ultimately returned through an exchange-shaped deposit account to rDAE53. Bitquery explicitly says the pattern fits one Binance customer rather than Binance itself.
records.limitations: The article does not state the exact PoR snapshot date/version used for the label and does not identify the wallet's XRP asset balance in the October 1 snapshot. It is a third-party label derived from a published list, not a direct official address-export row reproduced in the article. The bot cluster is behavioural attribution, not beneficial-owner identity.

records.title: 185,017,485 XRP transferred from Binance to unknown wallet — 29 October 2026
records.summary: Whale Alert identifies transaction 78E31E7BB06ADABE2322FDD0553533873C1D90664AEDE0C12DE06208F50BFA6A at 20:05 UTC on 29 October: approximately 185,017,485 XRP (the alert rounds to whole XRP; Bithomp's prior account record preserves 185,017,485.5 XRP) moved from Binance-labelled rDAE53VfMvftPB4ogpWGWvzkQxfht6JPxr to rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. Whale Alert valued the transfer at approximately $235.8M using $1.2703/XRP.
records.limitations: Alert rounds the XRP amount and uses its own price mark. It identifies the receiver as unknown and does not independently prove the sender's beneficial owner, PoR snapshot membership or legal characterization; the exact validated-ledger transaction remains the controlling evidence.

records.title: Act on Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Companies, Article 2

records.title: SBIC investment-development free seminar — The Present and Future of Generative AI (ChatGPT), 26 February 2025
records.summary: Tokyo SBIC's official program advertises a 26 February 2025 seminar titled 'The Present and Future of Generative AI (ChatGPT)'. It says the speaker was Microsoft Japan executive/evangelist Tetsuhiro Nishiwaki, with a ChatGPT demonstration. The event was co-hosted by Tokyo SBIC and the Tokyo Chamber of Commerce and Industry Taito branch, with Japan Finance Corporation Tokyo and Ueno branches as supporters.
records.limitations: This documents an educational seminar about ChatGPT, not a partnership with OpenAI, a ChatGPT product integration, an equity investment or an XRP/blockchain initiative.
